newsitem.title: ITALY: OECD says Italy deficit target "credible" - govt.
newsitem.headline: OECD says Italy deficit target "credible" - govt.

text.p: The OECD sees Italy's bid to reduce the ratio between its deficit and gross domestic product to three percent in 1997 as "credible," the Italian government said in a statement.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's office said the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) estimated the ratio would be 3.7 percent next year but said this forecast did not take account for all of Italy's planned budget measures.
"Reaching a three percent ratio between deficit and GDP is therefore seen as credible, even in a context of noticeably lower growth than expected," the government statement said.

It said leaks of a forthcoming OECD report, due to be published next week, quoted the Paris-based organisation as saying that the economy would grow by just 1.2 percent next year against a government target of two percent.

Earlier on Wednesday, employers' organisation Confindustria said Italy would fall well short of the three-percent deficit/GDP target and warned that without a mini-budget early next year, the ratio would be 4.8 percent.
"The government just wants to say that international institutions like the OECD and European Commission differ strongly from Confindustria's pessimistic outlook," the statement said.
The European Commission forecast earlier this year that Italy's deficit/GDP ratio in 1997 would be 3.3 percent, but like the OECD, it did not take into account all the government's budget plans.

Under the terms of the Maastricht Treaty, countries wishing to sign up to the planned European single currency in 1999 need to have a deficit/GDP ratio of three percent in 1997. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
